name: Franklin Pike
life: “I still remember carrying a cupboard while somebody cried behind it.” Thursday often includes a stop at the approach to Seabright Court, where Franklin likes to watch the beach traffic thin enough for workers going the other way.
voice: I offered boxes and got asked to be a witness at the lease meeting. I'm wearing my good shoes for that.
appearance: Franklin has a broad nose and a deep dimple on one cheek. Look for black hair twisted into a small knot. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a gray fisher's sweater with a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. In conversation Franklin looks toward the door whenever a name is called.
personality: Franklin tells a better story in a kitchen than at a microphone. Family members sometimes underestimate how far Franklin will go to back a quiet opinion once it is actually challenged.
agenda: To stand beside the family at the lease meeting.
family: Darcy Fadel is Franklin’s half-sibling. Franklin picks the meeting place. Darcy sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The worker who couldn't read the joke*, Darcy says, “I laughed because my boss looked right at me.”
connections: Hollis Wick. A housing swap takes somebody willing to carry furniture and witness the paperwork.

reactions.situation: A relative offers the family a sofa with conditions
reactions.response: Franklin asks what using the sofa would mean for the people already living there.

reactions.situation: A friend asks for a loan due back before payday
reactions.response: Franklin agrees on a sum and a date with the friend in private, keeping the arrangement out of family gossip.

reactions.situation: If a relative makes a joke at a child's expense
reactions.response: Franklin repeats the child's actual point and waits for a reply to that.
